title: Quickstart Mini-Sprint: Hackbench + Failure Mode Manifest
content:
Purpose
This doc captures a compact lab-oriented quickstart (mini-sprint) for new SDK adopters and internal DEX (developer experience) engineers: a hands-on hackbench with explicit smoke tests and a prioritized failure-mode checklist. Aim is to produce a 90–180 minute workshop run by an engineer or solutions rep that ends with a validated sample app + telemetry signals for diagnosing common integration regressions.

Audience
- New integrator engineers trying Redwood SDKs for the first time
- DevEx engineers running onboarding workshops
- Solutions engineers preparing a demo for an early customer POC

Constraints & guiding principles
- Keep friction under 15 minutes of setup for the 30-minute quickstart path (credentials, install).
- Make failure modes visible: map errors to remediation steps and telemetry markers.
- Prefer reproducible, minimal sample apps (single-file Node and Python) and short prompts.
- Instrument everything: event names, error tags, latency buckets, token counts.

Run formats (pick one)
- Lightning (30m): install -> hello-gen -> basic telemetry smoke -> done.
- Workshop (90m): include retry/backoff lab, streaming, function-calling sample, basic evals.
- Deep (2–3h): add embedding retrieval example, batching config, and quantization tradeoff doc link.

Manifest: artifacts to deliver
1) Hello sample (0-install path): single JS file using CDN-like snippet + example prompt.
2) Minimal Python quickstart (requirements.txt) with env var-based key loading.
3) Smoke test script (bash/python) that runs 6 checks and returns exit codes.
4) Telemetry checklist + example events (to paste into console onboarding).
5) Failure-mode playbook: top 8 errors with triage steps.
6) One-page facilitator guide: timings, talking points, troubleshooting tips.
7) GitHub PR template for sample updates and telemetry regressions.

Smoke tests (must be runnable locally)
- S1: SDK install works (npm/pip) -> exit 0.
- S2: Auth handshake (invalid key returns 401 + well-formed error object).
- S3: Basic generation returns tokens within expected size (not empty).
- S4: Streaming endpoint delivers chunks in <1500ms first-chunk on 95% runs (synthetic).
- S5: Embedding call returns vector length consistent with model spec.
- S6: Rate-limit response includes retry-after header and mapped telemetry event.

Failure-mode matrix (priority ordered)
- F1: Missing/incompatible SDK version -> symptom: import/require errors. Short fix: pin version in quickstart and add preflight script that prints SDK version. Telemetry marker: sdk.version_check_failed.
- F2: Bad API key / key rotated -> symptom: 401/403. Fix: env var checker + clear error message + redirect to console. Telemetry marker: auth.failure.
- F3: Network egress blocked (VPC/Firewall) -> symptom: connection timeout or DNS error. Fix: docs snippet with hostnames/ports, curl test. Telemetry: network.timeout.
- F4: Unexpected model response shape (e.g., streaming vs single payload) -> symptom: JSON parse errors. Fix: parse guard + fallback to non-stream path. Telemetry: parse.error.
- F5: Rate-limited in bursts -> symptom: 429. Fix: exponential backoff sample + circuit breaker. Telemetry: rate.limit.hit.
- F6: Large prompt -> OOM on local sim or extremely long latency on some model variants. Fix: prompt truncation sample + tokenize counter. Telemetry: prompt.too_long.
- F7: Telemetry not appearing in Console -> symptom: events sent but not visible. Fix: ensure ingestion key & dataset are correct, sample verify endpoint. Telemetry: telemetry.missing.
- F8: Embedding mismatch after model swap -> symptom: vector drift / length mismatch. Fix: add model-version check in preflight. Telemetry: model.mismatch.

Instrumentation checklist (developer-facing)
- Emit: onboarding.start, onboarding.complete, sample.run.error (with error.code), sample.run.latency (ms), sdk.version, model.name, model.version, token.count.input, token.count.output.
- Tag errors with: env (dev/prod), route (quickstart-hello), participant_id (anonymous session id).
- Provide tiny snippet to paste in apps to surface the above events.

Facilitator guide (30m lightning outline)
- 0–5m: Intros + goals. Confirm attendee env (node/python).
- 5–12m: Install + preflight (run preflight script).
- 12–20m: Hello generation + streaming demo (show raw chunks).
- 20–25m: Run smoke-test script and explain results.
- 25–30m: Wrap + next steps: embedder sample & follow-on deep workshop.

Preflight script (notes)
- Check node/python present and version.
- NPM/PIP install sanity check (can install packages offline if configured).
- Try a quick auth probe (small HEAD to /v0/health or similar).

Open questions / TODOs
- Which exact model should be the default for quickstart? (cost/latency tradeoffs). Suggestion: a small LLM variant verified in Redwood catalog.
- Do we include a local emulator fallback (for airgapped demos)? If yes, produce a 1-file stub server.
- Should the streaming demo always be included in lightning? streaming raises network flakiness risk. Option: include as opt-in.
- Need to coordinate with Console team for telemetry event names and retention defaults.

Links & references (for implementer)
- Confluence page (placeholder): CONFLUENCE-DEX-QUICKSTART (link to be created).
- Linear ticket: DEVEXP-4913 (linked_artifacts above).
- SDK sample PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-samples/pull/218

Notes to self (choppy):
- Keep code samples under 40 lines where possible. People skim.
- Add a "fast-fix" section in playbook for the 5 most common errors (map to F1..F5).
- Make a 1-click runbook in Console to replay smoke tests for a customer account (longer-term).
- Record a 12m screencast of the lightning run for Sales to reference.

Acceptance criteria for merging into samples repo
- Minimal JS + Python samples both pass local smoke tests on mac/linux (CI runs).
- Preflight script returns exit 0 with a valid key and prints SDK+model version.
- Telemetry events show up in Console with correct schema within 5 minutes.

Appendix: quick cheat commands (draft)
- Install (node): npm i @redwood-inference/sdk
- Run preflight (node): node ./preflight-check.js
- Run smoke tests: ./smoke-test.sh
- View PR: gh pr view 218 --repo redwood-inference/sdk-samples

End of doc.
